transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Scheduled duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood), Priya Patel (Redwood), Dana R. (BlueForge VP Eng), Marcus L. (DevOps), Sofia G. (ML), Harpreet S. (InfoSec), Tom A. (PM)

Summary:
Quick implementation onramp: walkthrough of runbook, network + security intake, staging plan, and a canary timeline for embeddings and chat flows. Discussed hosted vs dedicated considerations and initial success metrics.

Topics:
- Runbook and terraform snippets
- Network requirements (VPC, egress, firewall rules)
- SSO/KMS and audit logging expectations
- Canary strategy and evaluation metrics (latency, cost, quality)
- Timeline to staging + pilot

Action items (also in metadata): see list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. just to confirm we've got about 50 minutes, we want to run through the onboarding runbook, get net ops details, and lock a pilot week.
[00:12] Dana Rivera: yep thanks. we'll be short on time later so appreciate the focus. Marcus and Harpreet are here for infra and security.
[00:20] Priya Patel: great, i'll share my screen in a sec, i'll go over the runbook and sample terraform snippets for the private deployment path and hosted fallbacks.
[00:30] Marcus Lin: quick question before you start — we run a mix of public cloud and some colo, is the private package able to support a hybrid network with NATed egress?
[00:40] Priya Patel: yes, the private on-prem/VPC package supports NAT egress patterns. we typically ask for the CIDR blocks and egress proxies. there is a small NAT requirement for model downloads during initial setup unless you use an airgap bundle.
[00:56] Tom Alvarez: airgap bundle? in case we need to. can you give the tradeoffs?
[01:02] Priya Patel: airgap means we'll hand over an installer artifact — no outbound calls at all. tradeoff is manual model upgrades and longer ops to patch. recommended for regulated customers. for most, VPC with strict egress and proxying is smoother.
[01:20] Sofia Gomez: for our initial use case we want embeddings for search and a chat assistant for dev docs. targets: embeddings latency under 25ms median and chat responses under 350ms token stream. are those realistic?
[01:34] Liam Chen: that depends on hosted vs dedicated and model choice. for hosted with the curated medium model you might be ~30-60ms per embedding depending on batch sizes; dedicated GPUs will hit latency SLOs more consistently.
[01:48] Marcus Lin: are those numbers per request in our infra or after network hop? need to understand network-add.
[01:55] Priya Patel: good call — metrics in the runbook are token generation time at the runtime; add network round-trip for public cloud egress. we include tracing hooks in the console so you can split where time is spent.
[02:10] Harpreet Singh: on security — we need details on KMS integration, where keys are stored, and if Redwood keeps any model artifacts. also SOC2 and audit logs.
[02:21] Liam Chen: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSM). for hosted we offer envelope encryption and do not retain plaintext model inputs beyond configured retention. we do provide audit logs for all admin actions; i'll send the SOC2 summary and the audit schema.
[02:37] Harpreet Singh: sounds good. also need to validate data residency — some of our customer data must remain in eu-west-1. is region pinning supported?
[02:46] Priya Patel: yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. hosted API has regional endpoints; for strict residency you'd want a dedicated pool or private deployment in the desired region.
[02:58] Dana Rivera: wanted to raise cost to performance — would we expect to start hosted and then move to dedicated once usage grows?
[03:06] Liam Chen: that's a common pattern. start on hosted for fast iteration, then move to Dedicated when you need predictable throughput. Redwood supports model pinning during the migration so you won't see behavioral surprises.
[03:18] Marcus Lin: migration plan — is there a downtime window?
[03:22] Priya Patel: we do canary migrations with traffic mirroring and cutover. typical plan is a canary with a percentage of traffic, validate metrics, then shift. negligible downtime; we add fallbacks to hosted in case capacity issues arise.
[03:36] Tom Alvarez: what about developer workflow? our devs want the same API surface during both hosted and private.
[03:41] Liam Chen: same API surface across modes — that's one of the core pieces. SDKs are identical and we surface model versions so you can pin in CI.
[03:50] Sofia Gomez: about evals — can Redwood run a quick perf/quality eval with our prompts? we could share 50 representative prompts.
[03:58] Priya Patel: absolutely, we recommend sharing 50-200 prompts for a baseline. we'll run them on the suggested model, provide latency/cost/quality metrics, and show quantization/throughput tradeoffs.
[04:12] Marcus Lin: network intake — what specifically do you need? I'll summarize now but please add to the action items.
[04:17] Priya Patel: primarily: VPC CIDRs, subnet mapping, NAT details, egress proxies, firewall rules for outbound endpoints, and service accounts for any S3 or blob access. sample terraform snippets are in the runbook.
[04:32] Marcus Lin: got it. we use strict egress via proxy, so we'll have to test the model download flow and maybe do an explicit allow for S3 endpoints.
[04:42] Priya Patel: yes also note: if you go with the private package, we can do pre-seed model artifacts via a secure transfer to your staging bucket to avoid open egress.
[04:55] Harpreet Singh: question on logs — are logs PII redacted automatically? and can we configure retention?
[05:02] Liam Chen: we offer token-level redaction options in the runtime; retention windows are configurable and audit logs are separate. we'll include the retention and redaction controls in the runbook doc.
[05:14] Tom Alvarez: timeline: what's realistic to get to a staging canary for embeddings?
[05:19] Priya Patel: with the artifacts ready (VPC, creds, sample prompts) we can stand up staging in about 5 business days. pilot/validation ~1-2 weeks after that depending on eval scope.
[05:31] Dana Rivera: that works. next items — mapping stakeholders for the pilot and success criteria.
[05:36] Liam Chen: success criteria typically: embeddings median latency <= X ms, recall lift over baseline Y%, and cost per 1k queries under Z. we can co-author the exact numbers after Sofia shares prompts.
[05:48] Sofia Gomez: for recall lift baseline is our current elasticsearch-based sim search. expecting 10-15% R@10 improvement.
[05:56] Priya Patel: noted, we'll include the eval template.
[06:02] [Screen share begins — Priya walks through runbook]
[06:12] Priya Patel: here's the runbook top-level — preflight, network, infra, deployment, smoke tests, observability, rollback. the terraform snippets are under /examples.
[06:26] Marcus Lin: I see an example for AWS — we are multi-cloud so will need GCP snippets too, do you have them?
[06:33] Priya Patel: yes gcp snippets are in the repo but we can flag the ones most relevant to your pattern.
[06:40] Tom Alvarez: curious about autoscaling — what controls are available?
[06:44] Liam Chen: autoscaling in Dedicated is based on queued tokens and latency. you can define min/max instance and concurrency targets. for private you can use same autoscaling hooks tied to your kube or node pools.
[06:58] Harpreet Singh: any SOC2 artifacts you can share?
[07:02] Liam Chen: yes i'll attach our SOC2 summary, MAA, and the security whitepaper.
[07:10] Harpreet Singh: good — and can we have an NDA/BAA as well? procurement will need that.
[07:16] Liam Chen: yes procurement templates are in the shared folder, i'll drop a BAA and an SOW template.
[07:24] [08:00] Sofia Gomez: on the embeddings canary — do you recommend batching on the client or rely on Redwood's batching?
[08:08] Priya Patel: both — client batching helps reduce latency variance; our runtime does continuous batching for small requests. we can show the batching benefit in the eval results.
[08:19] Marcus Lin: FYI we have a bursty pattern at certain times of day — need to understand how the runtime behaves under totally spikey load.
[08:26] Liam Chen: we can run stress tests in staging to mimic spikes. Dedicated with reserved capacity smooths the tail latency.
[08:34] Tom Alvarez: what's the expected cost delta between hosted and dedicated for steady traffic? ballpark?
[08:40] Priya Patel: it depends on utilization. hosted is variable, dedicated has a fixed commit. if you have predictable steady throughput, dedicated amortizes better. we'll provide a sample cost model for your projected QPS.
[08:53] [10:00] Dana Rivera: can you walk through observability — how do we debug slow requests?
[10:07] Priya Patel: console exposes per-route latency, token breakdown, and tracing hooks. you'll see token gen time, queue time, kernel exec time. we provide SLO alerts and traces you can forward to your tracing stack.
[10:21] Marcus Lin: about traces — do you inject any headers we need to catch correlation ids?
[10:25] Liam Chen: we accept X-Request-Id and propagate it through the runtime. SDKs set this automatically if present.
[10:32] Harpreet Singh: data in transit — is mTLS supported between Redwood agent and control plane?
[10:37] Priya Patel: yes we support mTLS for agent-control plane comms and mutual auth for private installs.
[10:44] Sofia Gomez: small nit — we saw mention of K-V cache in a doc but our infra team misread it as K-V cash — can you clarify how KV caching works and where the cache lives?
[10:55] Priya Patel: ha, K-V cache is key-value cache for attention KV states; in private, it's local to the runtime node; for hosted it's ephemeral in the runtime tier and not persisted to disk. we'll add an explanatory diagram.
[11:12] Marcus Lin: great.
[11:15] [15:00] Liam Chen: quick recap — we have concrete next steps: runbook + terraform (Priya), network details (Marcus), prompts and success criteria (Sofia), SOC2/KMS info (Liam/Harpreet). aim for a staging spin-up by next week if artifacts are ready.
[15:33] Tom Alvarez: procurement lead will get the BAA to us. once that's signed we can exchange creds for staging.
[15:40] Liam Chen: perfect. Priya, any gotchas for the staging access we should call out?
[15:45] Priya Patel: ensure service account has least privilege to the staging bucket and the NAT allows model object retrieval if not pre-seeded. also open egress to the specific endpoints if you prefer not to pre-seed.
[16:00] Dana Rivera: anything else on timelines?
[16:03] Liam Chen: target: runbook + network details this week, staging spin up next week, pilot canary first week of June.
[16:12] Sofia Gomez: noted. I'll upload prompt sets and expected evaluation metrics by Friday.
[16:18] Harpreet Singh: I'll send compliance checklist and any extra controls.
[16:22] [50:00] wrap — brief signoff
[50:10] Liam Chen: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the runbook link and SOC2 artifacts, and we'll get the staging slot on the calendar.
[50:18] Marcus Lin: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.

References shared in call notes:
- Runbook link: (shared via Redwood drive) "blueforge-runbook-v1.pdf"
- Terraform examples: /examples/aws and /examples/gcp (noted in runbook)
